name: RJ45 / 8P8C (Ethernet)
description: The 8-contact modular connector used for twisted-pair Ethernet. Contacts are numbered 1-8 with the tab/latch facing away and the gold pins toward you. Wiring follows T568A or T568B (this entry lists T568B, the common one); the two schemes just swap the orange and green pairs, and either works as long as both ends match. 10/100 Ethernet uses only pins 1,2,3,6; Gigabit uses all four pairs.
variants: T568A vs T568B: the two swap the orange and green pairs (pins 1/2 <-> 3/6). Both are valid; a cable with T568A on one end and T568B on the other is a crossover cable.
10/100 (Fast Ethernet) uses only pairs on 1-2 (TX) and 3-6 (RX); 4/5 and 7/8 are unused. Gigabit (1000BASE-T) uses all four pairs bidirectionally.
gotchas: Pairs are 1-2, 3-6, 4-5, 7-8. Note pin 3 pairs with 6 (not 4/5) -- splitting the 3-6 pair across two twists kills the signal at speed. This trips up hand-crimped cables.
PoE (Power over Ethernet) injects DC on the pairs: Mode A on the data pairs (1-2 / 3-6), Mode B on the spare pairs (4-5 / 7-8) for 10/100. Do not probe a live PoE port expecting 0 V.
Modern gear is auto-MDI-X, so straight-through vs crossover no longer matters between switches/PCs -- but older equipment still needs the right cable.
notes: 8P8C pinout per ANSI/TIA-568 with the T568B colour code and 1000BASE-T pair assignments; universal.
